summary: A target-level integration of the umbrella T.3 stage. Native valuation-ring unit parts realize the existing tame pairing; an explicit normalization dictionary and degree-two map square connect it to higher Milnor residues and the actual localization boundary. All higher constructions, finite-support and transfer results retain their existing owners. Coverage is planned, with the inherited field, localization/product and generic complete-DVR inputs recorded as gaps; no implementation or closure is asserted.

nodes.title: Native unit parts
nodes.statement: For π∈Fˣ with ord_v(π)=1 and f∈Fˣ, define U_π(f)∈Rˣ to be the unique unit whose field value is f·π^(−ord_v(f)). Obtain its data by choosing the witness in Valuation.exists_eq_zpow_mul_unit_of_surjective after installing Valuation.nontrivial_valueGroup_of_surjective and translating ord_v(π)=1 to v.IsUniformizer(π). This is a native-carrier adapter to the unit decomposition used by the existing tame-symbol owner, rather than a new valuation ring or symbol presentation.
hypotheses: F is a field; v:F→ℤᵐ⁰ is a surjective valuation, R=v.valuationSubring and k=IsLocalRing.ResidueField R. Write ord_v(f)=−log(v(f)) for nonzero f.
proofSteps: Use the existing existential decomposition to select an actual element of Rˣ. No axiom or missing data construction is needed for this adapter.
Cancel π^ord_v(f) in F to identify the selected unit with fπ^(−ord_v(f)); injectivity of R→F and of units→R proves uniqueness.
Use ord_mul and ord_zpow to obtain the multiplicative and power laws; cancellation also identifies the effect of replacing π by cπ.
acceptance: The maps have the displayed native domains and codomains, and every equality uses the specified residue normalization.

sources.match: The symbol and specialization formulas use the unit factors of uniformizer expansions; the library already provides their existence.

nodes.title: Native realization of the tame symbol
nodes.statement: Let f,g∈Fˣ, a=ord_v(f), b=ord_v(g), π∈Fˣ of order one, and write r:Rˣ→kˣ for Units.map(IsLocalRing.residue R). The native expression T_π(f,g)=(−1)^(ab) r(U_π(f))^b r(U_π(g))^(−a) equals the existing tameSymbol_v(f,g). If z∈Rˣ has field value f^b g^(−a), then T_π(f,g)=(−1)^(ab)r(z). Such z exists because its field value has order zero. Consequently the expression agrees with the existing uniformizer-free implementation through R.unitGroupMulEquiv and is independent of π. This is an equality of pairings on Fˣ×Fˣ before any K-group quotient.
hypotheses: F is a field; v:F→ℤᵐ⁰ is a surjective valuation, R=v.valuationSubring and k=IsLocalRing.ResidueField R. Write ord_v(f)=−log(v(f)) for nonzero f.
proofSteps: Substitute f=π^a U_π(f) and g=π^b U_π(g). In f^b g^(−a), the π exponents cancel exactly, for arbitrary integers a,b.
The native unit factors identify z with U_π(f)^b U_π(g)^(−a). Apply the existing residue homomorphism; its definition through unitGroupMulEquiv gives the comparison to the predecessor formula.

Changing π to cπ introduces c^(−ab) and c^(ab), which cancel. Import the established bilinear/Steinberg proof plan and arbitrary valued-embedding ramification formula; no second quotient or ramification theory is constructed.
acceptance: For f=1/5 and g=4/5, the negative-order Steinberg test gives 1, including the sign.

Under a field embedding with positive ramification index e and the induced residue embedding, the target tame value is the e-th power of the mapped source tame value. Finite-dimensionality is not assumed.

sources.match: The source gives the inverse convention; invert its unit-factor expression and ramification identity to obtain this native realization.

nodes.title: Residue convention dictionary
nodes.statement: For every n≥1, let ∂^last_v:K^M_n(F)→K^M_(n−1)(k) be the existing residue normalized by ∂^last{u₁,…,u_(n−1),π}={ū₁,…,ū_(n−1)} and zero on all-unit symbols. Let ∂^first be the residue of Weibel III.7.3, normalized with π first. As homomorphisms, ∂^first_v=(−1)^(n−1)∂^last_v. In degree one both are ord_v; in degree two, under K^M_1(k)=kˣ, ∂^last is tameSymbolHom and ∂^first is its inverse. If d_π(x)=λ_π(x)+∂^last_v(x)Π in the existing Serre algebra, Π is on the right. For homogeneous x of degree i and y of degree j, ∂^last(xy)=λ_π(x)∂^last(y)+(−1)^j∂^last(x)ρ_π(y), where ρ_π{uπ^m}={(−1)^mū}. In the first normalization the corresponding law is ∂^first(xy)=(−1)^iλ_π(x)∂^first(y)+∂^first(x)ρ_π(y). For π′=cπ, λ_π′(x)=λ_π(x)−∂^last(x){c̄}, while ∂^last does not change.
hypotheses: F is a field; v:F→ℤᵐ⁰ is a surjective valuation, R=v.valuationSubring and k=IsLocalRing.ResidueField R. Write ord_v(f)=−log(v(f)) for nonzero f.
proofSteps: Use the existing Serre-algebra coefficient splitting, not a second construction. Moving Π past a degree-(n−1) coefficient gives the factor (−1)^(n−1), including the 2-torsion relation Π²={−1}Π.

Expand d_π(x)d_π(y) using the explicit multiplication of the imported Serre algebra. Its coefficient on the right is the displayed last-normalization product law; substitute the degree signs to obtain the first-normalization law.

Apply the existing automorphism Π↦Π−{c̄} to identify specialization under π′=cπ. The residue coefficient is unchanged. The degree-two value is fixed by {u,π}, not by an unlabelled abstract group isomorphism.
acceptance: In degree three both residues send {u₁,u₂,π} to {ū₁,ū₂}; in degree two they take inverse values on {2,5} at ord_5.
λ_5{5}=1 but λ_10{5}=3 in 𝔽_5ˣ. Independence of specialization would fail this test.
For x={5}, y={2}, the last-normalization product law gives 3 and the first-normalization law gives 2 in 𝔽_5ˣ.

nodes.title: The degree-two residue comparison square
nodes.statement: Let R be the native DVR, with fraction field F and residue field k. Write μ_F:K^M_2(F)≃K₂^St(F) for the imported Matsumoto equivalence, c_F:K₂^St(F)≃K₂^Q(F) for T.1/k2-pi2 followed by the imported plus=Q comparison, η_F=c_F∘μ_F, and det_k:K₁^Q(k)≃kˣ for the imported field determinant comparison. For the actual localization boundary B^R₂:K₂^Q(F)→K₁^Q(k), normalized by B₁[π]=1 and the right module rule B(x·j*y)=B(x)·i*y, the following equalities of homomorphisms hold: tameSymbolHom^M_v=tameSymbolHom^St_v∘μ_F=inv∘det_k∘B^R₂∘η_F. Also ∂^last_v in degree two agrees with tameSymbolHom^M_v under K^M_1(k)=kˣ. Setting B^L₂=−B^R₂ gives det_k∘B^L₂∘η_F=tameSymbolHom^M_v. Here inv denotes inversion of the abelian group kˣ. These equalities concern the actual symbol, product and connecting maps, not arbitrary chosen isomorphisms. The same inversion is applied at every prime in the Dedekind boundary and cancels from either norm/residue square.
hypotheses: F is a field; v:F→ℤᵐ⁰ is a surjective valuation, R=v.valuationSubring and k=IsLocalRing.ResidueField R. Write ord_v(f)=−log(v(f)) for nonzero f.
π∈Fˣ is a uniformizer of order one. The Milnor, classical, plus and Quillen identifications and the localization/product maps are the specified imported natural maps.
proofSteps: Import the actual connecting map from K.3 and its unit-product identification from K.7/T.2. Import det_k from U.3 through K.2:plus/zero-one-ring-comparison and c_F through T.1/k2-pi2 followed by K.2:plus/plus-equals-Q; the missing supplier contracts remain explicit gaps.
The degree-one index computation gives B₁[π]=1. The right module rule then gives det_k B₂([π]·[u])=ū. Graded commutativity and the symbol-product comparison give det_k B₂([u]·[π])=ū^(−1).

Expand arbitrary field entries into a uniformizer power times a ring unit. Bilinearity, the all-unit zero boundary and the relation {π,π}={π,−1} identify B₂ on every symbol with the inverse tame symbol. Symbol generation promotes this to equality of homomorphisms.

For a Dedekind domain restrict the actual sequence to each DVR; finite support gives the direct-sum map. Inversion is an automorphism of every residue unit group and commutes with residue norms, so both normalizations give the identical transfer square. Import, rather than reconstruct, the two transfer functors and their degree-two comparison.
acceptance: On {2,5} over ℚ at 5, tameSymbolHom has value 2, whereas det_k B^R₂ η has value 3. The square commutes only with the displayed inversion.
On {5,5}, both degree-two normalizations give −1, which is 4 in 𝔽_5; diagonal tests alone do not detect inversion.
For finite integral closure S/R, both the Milnor and Quillen norm/residue squares have residue-field norms and no extra e_w factor. The restriction square has e_w instead.

sources.match: The index fixes the positive degree-one boundary, the product calculation identifies the degree-two boundary, and the finite-map diagram supplies its transfer compatibility.

Apply the existing abelian-localization, dévissage and resolution nodes to this equivalence. For every field F and a,b∈Fˣ, prove that the ordered Quillen product [a]·[b] equals c_F(μ_F{a,b}) under the existing T.1 plus comparison and the T.2 field-symbol normalization. gaps.title: G-T3-localization: the ring localization application
gaps.detail: The generic K.3 abelian localization, dévissage and resolution nodes exist as plans, but its explicit identification of the quotient of finitely generated R-modules by the torsion Serre subcategory with finite-dimensional F-vector spaces is still the inherited requested application. The degree-one index and right product-boundary nodes are cited directly and are not missing baseline declarations. Supply the ring application before declaring the actual Dedekind sequence closed.

gaps.title: G-T3-product: product-symbol compatibility
gaps.detail: The Quillen product of the ordered unit classes [a]·[b] must equal the image of the chosen classical symbol under T.1/k2-pi2. K.7 owns products and T.2 owns the graded map; this exact square remains the inherited product-symbol request. Neither Matsumoto alone nor a free choice of group isomorphism supplies it.

gaps.title: G-T3-generic-DVR: precise incomplete supplier routing
gaps.detail: The predecessor routes finite extensions of complete DVR fraction fields with arbitrary residue field to a proposed, unregistered LocalFieldsRamification Part II (its restructure.supportPlan, DVR.0–DVR.3). The needed exports are extension valuations, finite integral-closure lattices and their rank, valuation/residue norm identities including inseparable residue extensions, and tensor-component lengths for arbitrary scalar extension. The finite-integral-closure completion product used in the general norm proof also remains an exact supplier request. Current AlgebraicCurves Layers 5 and 9 already own completion/valuation-ring/residue/uniformizer compatibility and coefficient expansions at arbitrary residue field; import those targets in their stated generality and do not re-plan them in the proposed Part II. Current LocalFieldsRamification finite-local-field results do not imply the missing generic extension/norm contracts. Registration must preserve this division of ownership and assign only the missing exports to their supplier. No claim is made to have freshly read or completed the Gille–Szamuely proof cited by the imported norm node.

gaps.title: G-T3-field-comparison: inherited field-presentation closure
gaps.detail: The actual μ_F and c_F are imported from T.2/matsumoto and T.1/k2-pi2 followed by K.2:plus/plus-equals-Q. The T.2 umbrella continuation records inherited stable-colimit and centrality gaps and ordinary Bruhat/root-coordinate refinements. This T.3 integration does not close those proofs or replace them with an abstract symbol-preserving isomorphism assumed as data. The elementary native pairing does not depend on this gap. In particular T.1/k2-pi2 retains G-cover-Hurewicz: the explicit BE(F)-plus universal-cover comparison and natural Hurewicz map, compatible with the chosen plus/Q comparison, must be supplied by the existing K.2:plus and homotopy-theory owners. A generic existence theorem for a plus construction or an abstract isomorphism does not discharge this map-level input.

This is a completed target-level planning pass with T.3 planned, not closed: all four recorded supplier/proof gaps and both requests remain. The sources, all 18 baseline declarations, the 24 imported owner statements, target coverage, graph, API, tests and planet selection were independently checked. The two carried source findings have independent confirmed reviews. checked.reason: The native decomposition witness and its Nontrivial value-group prerequisite match the pins. The original suggested file omitted the packet’s multiplication, unit, change-of-uniformizer and residue-bridge API and its two concrete numerical tests. Added the missing signatures and exact test markers, split the integer-power API into its two named declarations, and used consistent namespace-qualified packet names. All eight API entries and three tests now have corresponding declarations/examples. The residue bridge closes by reflexivity.

Cancellation of the integer uniformizer powers identifies the native ring unit with f^ord(g)g^(−ord(f)). Reduction therefore has the correct native unit domain.
